A Scottish doctor, missionary and explorer, the most famous European in Africa in his day. He went to southern Africa for the London Missionary Society in 1841.

  • From 1853 to 1856 he crossed the continent, from Luanda on the Atlantic to Quelimane on the Indian Ocean.
  • In 1855 he became the first European to see the great falls on the Zambezi, which he named Victoria Falls after Queen Victoria.
  • His Zambezi expedition of 1858 to 1864 failed to open the river to shipping.
  • In his last years he searched for the source of the Nile. Henry Morton Stanley found him at Ujiji in 1871.

He saw the slave trade of the interior up close, and his reports helped push Britain to force the closing of the Zanzibar slave market in 1873. He died that year in what is now Zambia. His African companions carried his body to the coast, and he was buried in Westminster Abbey.
sum: A Scottish doctor, missionary and explorer, the most famous European in Africa in his day. He went to southern Africa for the London Missionary Society in 1841.
